newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Japan seeks talks with U.S. on photo-film RBP.
newsitem.headline: Japan seeks talks with U.S. on photo-film RBP.

text.p: Japan has asked for consultations with the United States on restrictive business practices (RBP) in the U.S. photo-film market, a Tokyo envoy said.
Nobutoshi Akao, Japan's ambassador to the World Trade Organisation, said the request was part of a response to a similar U.S. request concerning the Japanese photo-film market.
Both requests were outside the WTO dispute settlement procedure and were based on a 1960 agreement in the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) allowing for bilateral consultations on RBP.
The requests are linked to a wide-ranging dispute between the two countries and their photo-film giants -- Eastman Kodak and Fuji -- over access to the Japanese market.

Akao spoke to reporters after blocking a request from the U.S. for immediate creation of a WTO panel to study whether Japanese regulations favoured Fuji and deprived Kodak of equal access to Japanese consumers.
The panel, which will be asked to rule whether Japan was violating WTO rules on goods trade, will be set up automatically at the next meeting of the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body on October 16.
